candidate_readme:
# Agent trace

Exports the agent loop as an OpenTelemetry trace so eval harnesses and OTLP-aware viewers can see what a run actually did: turns, provider requests, tool calls, and compaction, with timings and token accounting.

## Usage

```bash
pi -e packages/coding-agent/examples/extensions/agent-trace
```

Or copy the directory to `~/.pi/agent/extensions/agent-trace` / `.pi/extensions/agent-trace` for auto-discovery.

## File

Spans are appended to:

```
<SessionManager.getSessionDir()>/traces/<session id>.otlp.jsonl
```

`PI_AGENT_TRACE_FILE` replaces that path when set. The file is JSON Lines; each line is one OTLP/JSON `ExportTraceServiceRequest` with a single span. A span is written twice: a start line (`pi.span.phase` = `"start"`, no end time or status) when it begins, and an end line (full attributes, `endTimeUnixNano`, `status`) when it finishes. The file only grows. Reloads and later processes resume the same session file and trace id.

## Spans

| name | kind | parent | when |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pi.run` | INTERNAL (1) | none, or the spawning tool in a sub-agent | one agent loop invocation (`agent_start` … `agent_end`) |
| `pi.turn` | INTERNAL | the run | one assistant response and its tool batch |
| `chat <model>` | CLIENT (3) | the turn | one provider request (not compaction summaries) |
| `execute_tool <tool>` | INTERNAL | the turn | one tool execution |
| `pi.compaction` | INTERNAL | none, or the spawning tool in a sub-agent | one compaction, from preparation to success or failure |

`pi.run.trigger` is `"prompt"`, `"wakeup"`, or `"continuation"`. Overflow retries set `pi.run.after_compaction` instead of a message entry id. Steering and in-run follow-ups are listed on the run as `pi.run.steer_entry_ids`; they do not open a new run.

Failed tools, aborted/error assistant responses, failed compactions, and spans closed by shutdown use status ERROR. A run stays OK even when a turn inside it failed.

## Sub-agents

While a traced tool is executing, the process sets:

- `PI_AGENT_TRACE_ID` — this session's trace id
- `PI_AGENT_TRACE_PARENT_SPAN_ID` — the executing tool's span id

A child `pi` inherits those variables and writes its own session file, but every span uses the parent's trace id and each child root span (`pi.run`, `pi.compaction`) is parented to the spawning tool. When no tool is executing, those variables are restored to the values the process started with.
